Basis: the general rule of liability for personal fault in the Civil Code (any act committed by a person through his fault that causes harm to another obliges the one who caused it to compensate) - check the wording as amended in 2005.
Abuse of a right as a form of fault (Civil Code article added in 2005): intent to harm, minor interest compared with the harm, or unlawful interest.
Element 1, fault: an act or omission of the defendant that departs from the conduct of a careful person (assault, negligence, defamation, destruction); state its date and place.

Element 2, harm: material harm (loss suffered and gain missed) and moral harm (any attack on liberty, honour or reputation, Civil Code article on moral damage added in 2005); harm must be certain, not merely possible.
Element 3, causation: a direct causal link between the fault and the harm; the defendant escapes by proving an external cause (force majeure, sudden event, fault of the victim or of a third party).
Capacity: liability of a person without discernment (minor, insane) - who answers, and the liability of those who supervise him.
Several persons responsible for the same harm: joint (in solidum) liability and the sharing between them.
Defences that remove fault: legitimate self-defence, obeying an order of a superior that had to be obeyed (public agent), state of necessity (reduced compensation).
Burden of proof: the victim proves fault, harm and causation; facts may be proved by any means (witnesses, presumptions), the writing rule does not apply to material facts.
Criminal conviction: effect of a final criminal judgment on the civil judge - binding only on facts it necessarily decided (fact, its attribution to the defendant, its legal description).

Criminal proceedings pending on the same facts: the civil judge must stay the civil claim until the criminal action is finally decided (criminal-procedure rule: the criminal holds the civil in abeyance).

Choice of route: the victim may join the criminal proceedings as civil party or sue before the civil court; the electa una via rule (once before the civil judge, he cannot go to the criminal court, unless the prosecution started after).

Assessment of compensation: the judge fixes it according to the general damages provisions (loss suffered and gain missed) taking account of the circumstances; he may reserve the victim's right to ask for a reassessment within a period when the harm cannot be finally fixed.
Form of compensation: money or in kind (restoring the previous state), lump sum or periodic income, with or without security.

Limitation: the action for compensation lapses after 15 years from the day the harmful act occurred (Civil Code, as amended 2005); check whether there is a shorter period in the older wording (3 years from knowledge).
Civil action resulting from an offence: lapses according to the Civil Code rules (criminal-procedure code as amended), not with the public action.
Limitation is not raised by the court of its own motion; only on a plea of the party; counting of periods by days, the first day not counted.
Interruption and suspension of limitation: judicial claim, acknowledgement by the debtor; suspension when there is an impediment to act.
Formal notice: not required when the obligation is compensation arising from a harmful act (Civil Code article on cases where notice is not needed).
No prior conciliation or administrative step is required before filing a tort claim before the civil section.
Competent section: the civil section of the tribunal (first instance court).

Territorial jurisdiction: in matters of compensation for a crime, offence, contravention or tortious act, the court in whose district the harmful act occurred (Code of civil and administrative procedure); otherwise the defendant's domicile.

Exit to administrative courts: when the harm is caused by the State, a wilaya, a commune or a public administrative body (public hospital, police) - administrative jurisdiction; exception for damage caused by vehicles of these bodies, which stays with ordinary courts.
Exit to the criminal judge: the victim may bring the civil action alongside the public action before the criminal court.
Boundary: harm caused by a thing in the defendant's custody (guardian of a thing), an animal or the collapse of a building - different regime (presumed liability), not this claim.
Boundary: road traffic accidents - compensation regime of Ordinance 74-15 (insurance, no-fault scale), not general tort.
Boundary: work accidents and occupational illnesses - social security regime (Law 83-13), social section.
Boundary: harm arising from breach of a contract between the parties - contractual liability, not tort.
Boundary: liability of the employer for the act of his employee (principal for agent) and of the supervisor for the minor - vicarious liability, different articles.
Boundary: product liability of the producer for a defective product (Civil Code article added in 2005).
Boundary: defamation through the press - press code rules and short limitation periods may apply.
Requests: damages with an amount (material and moral heads stated separately), costs, provisional execution where justified.
Interest: no legal interest on compensation between private persons (prohibition of interest between individuals); damages for delay only under conditions.
Documents: medical certificates and expert reports, police reports, the criminal judgment and its certificate of finality, invoices and proof of loss.
Petition formal elements: identities, court, summary of facts and means, signed by the lawyer, fees paid.
Expertise: the court may order a medical or technical expertise to assess the harm; the petition may ask for it.

Amendments to remember: Civil Code amended by Law 05-10 (2005) changed the fault article, added abuse of right, moral damage, product liability and changed the limitation article; Code of criminal procedure on the limitation of the civil action.
